The nonuniform-influence form generalizes the hazard, \[ \frac{dF(t)}{dt} = \big[p + q F(t)^{\delta}\big]\big[1 - F(t)\big], \tag{198.16}\] where \(\delta = 1\) recovers the Bass model, \(\delta \in (0,1)\) encodes a high initial imitation coefficient, and \(\delta > 1\) encodes delayed influence and hence a lower, later peak. Recency matters too: more recent adopters can exert stronger influence on later ones [@sharma1994a].

Replacement and multi-unit purchases. @balasubramanian1989 fold replacement and penetration growth into a single sales equation, \[ y(t) = \big[a + b X(t)\big]\big[\alpha\,\text{Pop}(t)\,P^{\beta}(t) - X(t)\big] + r(t) + e(t), \tag{198.17}\] where \(X(t)\) is units in use at the start of year \(t\) (dead units already replaced), \(r(t)\) the units needing replacement, \(P(t)\) a price index, \(\alpha\) the ultimate penetration at base price, \(\beta\) the price-change effect on ultimate penetration, and \(a\), \(b\) the innovation and imitation coefficients. @steffens2003a models multiple-unit purchases by a single household, while trial-repeat structure and cross-country variation furnish further extensions.

A sober evaluation is warranted: every one of these extensions still rests on a single driving mechanism—the dispersion of knowledge through word of mouth.

추정과 대안적 확산 모형

The OLS estimator of Equation 198.6 is a starting point, not a destination. Maximum likelihood avoids time-interval bias but underestimates standard errors [@schmittlein1982]. Nonlinear least squares [@srinivasan1986] yields flexible, time-interval-bias-free estimates with valid standard errors but is data-hungry. Hierarchical Bayesian methods enable parameter updating and borrow strength across products, provided the troublesome notion of “similar” products is operationalized—as @bayus1993 does with an explicit segmentation scheme. Adaptive stochastic techniques let parameters drift over time, as in the augmented Kalman filter of @xie1997, and genetic algorithms can locate global optima and reduce bias.

Alternative models challenge the contagion premise itself. On the side of alternative drivers, @golder1998 model affordability with a Cobb–Douglas sales function, \[ S = P^{\beta_1} \cdot I^{\beta_2} \cdot CS^{\beta_3} \cdot MP^{\beta_4} \cdot e^{\varepsilon}, \tag{198.18}\] where sales are a product of price \(P\), income \(I\), consumer sentiment \(CS\), and market presence \(MP\); @horsky1990 combines price, income, and word of mouth in a single growth model. A large literature models heterogeneity in aggregate diffusion [@roberts1988b; @oren1988; @Chatterjee_1990; @bemmaor1984; @song2003; @sinha1992; @karshenas1993], and a strategy literature models the supply side—entry, marketing mix, and location [@dekimpe2000a; @Van_den_Bulte_2001; @bronnenberg2004]. On the side of alternative phenomena, spatial diffusion distinguishes contagious, expansion, hierarchical, and relocation processes [@mahajan1979; @redmond2003; @garber2004], and entertainment products typically follow exponential decay rather than S-shaped growth [@eliashberg1994; @eliashberg2000; @elberse2003; @moe2002; @lee2003].

The turning points have their own modeling traditions, developed further in 도약과 파괴적 혁신. Takeoff, “the point of transition from the introduction stage to the growth stage” [@golder1997], has been operationalized as a threshold relative to category peers [@golder1997], as the first turning point of a fitted logistic curve, as the largest three-year sales increase, as an annual-percentage-change criterion [@agarwal2002a], as a threshold adapted for international markets [@stremersch2004], and as a 10–20% penetration rule of thumb [@garber2004]. Its drivers include price declines [@golder1997], firm entry that improves quality and infrastructure [@agarwal2002a], and venturesome national culture [@tellis2003], and it is modeled with proportional [@golder1997] or log-logistic [@tellis2003] hazards—so far only on successful innovations. Slowdown, the transition from growth to maturity [@golder1997], is operationalized as the first of two consecutive post-takeoff years of below-peak sales [@golder2004] and explained by a dual-market split between early adopters and the early majority [@goldenberg2001], by negative informational cascades, and by affordability [@golder2004], using cellular-automata [@goldenberg2001] and hazard [@golder2004] models.

함수형 및 롱테일 확산

A productive modern move treats the entire penetration curve, not its parameters, as the unit of analysis. @sood2009 apply functional data analysis: yearly cumulative penetration for each category becomes a function, smoothed from discrete observations with splines (and, where data are sparse, with other smoothness-inducing devices that allow two or three time points to suffice). Functional principal components, functional regression, and functional cluster analysis then exploit the curve’s shape and borrow information across products and countries. The augmented functional regression integrates information across categories and so outperforms parametric extrapolation models, with product-specific effects more predictive of penetration than country-specific ones; the framework forecasts the years to takeoff and the timing and level of peak marginal penetration. The pedagogical virtue of the paper—telling a story from a simple model to progressively richer ones to justify each improvement—is itself worth emulating; its limits are the absence of formal hypotheses and its use of only same-category curves to predict a new product.

@appel2019 overturn the universality of the S-curve in long-tail digital markets. Studying SourceForge open-source software (excluding inactive projects and those with fewer than 200 downloads, in a market with a Gini coefficient of 0.96), they find that only the most popular products trace the familiar S-shape; lower-popularity products follow an exponential-like decline from launch (a “slide”) or a combination of slide and bell (“S&B”). The prior literature’s pro-innovation bias—the correlation between success and the importance assigned to a new product in development research—had concealed these patterns. The proposed inception model adds a heightened, time-decaying external influence, \[ p(t) = p\,e^{\delta t}, \tag{198.19}\] capturing influences not mediated by prior adopters—marketing mix, social-media posts, recommendations, expert opinion, influencers—that are strong early and decay. Methodologically, the analysis scales each pattern to \((0,1)\) by dividing by total downloads, smooths with a Hodrick–Prescott filter, and classifies shapes with a peaks-and-troughs algorithm; the same patterns recur in smartphone-app downloads. The key relationship is that higher popularity is associated with a lower share of adoptions due to the inception effect, so that inception is typically necessary but not sufficient for popularity. The analogy to movies (exponential blockbuster decline) and to supermarkets (heavy investment, little social influence) fails because the product types and the popularity–shape mapping differ.

마케팅과 채택 시점

When the outcome of interest is when an individual adopts rather than how a market diffuses, the natural object is the time to adoption. @prins2007 study the effects of direct and mass marketing on the adoption timing of a new e-service among existing customers, using 25 months of data on roughly 6,000 customers of a Dutch telecom operator. Adoption timing is “the time between the introduction and the adoption of the new service” [@steenkamp2003a], and switchers to a competitor’s service are treated as non-adopters—valid given the focus on the focal firm’s new service among existing customers. The findings are that advertising (including competitors’) shortens time to adoption and that mass marketing has a greater effect on loyal customers than direct marketing does. The design relies on a result of @donkers2003: absent stratification on the independent variables, oversampling rare events does not bias parameter estimates or standard errors in binary-choice models—a useful licence for studying infrequent adoption.

관련 논의

Two further studies sit naturally beside the diffusion literature. @tellis2020 find, in a large analysis of video advertising, that emotion outperforms information and that surprise and humor are effective yet underused, while explicit branding tends to hurt even as it is heavily deployed—with the caveat that the very rarity of these emotional tactics may be the source of their effectiveness, so that universal adoption could erode it. @Chandrasekaran_2020 extend generational diffusion to the problem of disruptive technological change; we treat that model in detail in 자기잠식과 파괴 상황에서의 생존 because its central construct is cannibalization.

도약과 파괴적 혁신

We study takeoff in part because new products tend to either take off or die—we rarely observe protracted flat sales—so the managerial decision reduces to a bet on whether takeoff will occur. Modeling the hazard of takeoff (the conditional probability of taking off given survival to date) is therefore the natural framing, and the hazard function typically peaks several years after introduction, so credible inference requires waiting at least that long.

파괴적 기술

The disruption thesis holds that incumbents fail by staying too close to their current customers while neglecting future ones. For each industry, a performance trajectory tracks how a technology improves relative to what the market demands. A sustaining technology maintains the established rate of improvement on the dimensions incumbents already serve; a disruptive technology underperforms on those dimensions initially but overshoots a different, initially marginal segment and eventually invades the mainstream. The prescriptive response is a sequence of diagnostic questions—Is the technology disruptive or sustaining? What is its strategic significance? Where is its initial market?—and an organizational answer: house the disruptive technology in a separate unit insulated from the incumbent’s current-customer pressures.

위험 모형을 이용한 도약 예측

@golder1997 make the prediction of takeoff operational. The key insight is a threshold: if base sales are small, a large percentage increase is needed to take off, whereas if base sales are large, a small percentage increase suffices, so the takeoff threshold is itself a function of base sales. Takeoff is then “the first year in which an individual category’s growth rate relative to base sales crosses this threshold”—equivalently, “the point of transition from the introductory stage to the growth stage of the product life cycle.” Operationally, the threshold is a plot of the percentage sales increase relative to base sales that demarcates takeoff. With price, year of introduction, market penetration, and product-specific and economic controls as covariates, the analysis finds that price at takeoff is below price at introduction, that average time to takeoff is about six years, that penetration at takeoff is about 1.7%, and that products tend to take off around the salient price points of $1{,}000, $500, and $100.

The estimator is Cox’s proportional-hazards model, \[ h_i(t) = h(t; z_{it}) = h_0(t)\,\exp\!\big(z_{it}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\beta}\big), \tag{198.20}\] where \(h_0(t)\) is an unspecified baseline hazard, \(z_{it}\) are the (possibly time-varying) covariates, and \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) is estimated by partial likelihood, leaving \(h_0(t)\) unparameterized. Two modeling choices deserve scrutiny: \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) is constrained equal across all categories, and unobserved heterogeneity (a frailty term) is excluded on the grounds that each takeoff event is unique and non-repeated—defensible for non-repeated events but a constraint to flag. The samples comprise eleven classic consumer durables, ten recently introduced durables, and ten categories evaluated during review; performance is assessed by a \(U^2\) reduction-in-uncertainty measure and by forecasts made at introduction and one year ahead.

NoteThe proportional-hazards assumption and what breaks it

Equation 198.20 imposes that covariates scale the baseline hazard multiplicatively and proportionally over time: the hazard ratio between two products with covariate vectors \(z\) and \(z'\) is \(\exp\!\big((z - z')^{\top}\boldsymbol{\beta}\big)\), constant in \(t\). If a covariate’s effect grows or fades over the product life cycle—plausible for price as a category matures—the proportionality assumption fails and \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\) is biased. Remedies include time-varying coefficients, stratified baselines, or the parametric (log-logistic) hazards used for international takeoff in @tellis2003. Pooling \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) across heterogeneous categories, as in @golder1997, trades efficiency for a homogeneity assumption that should be tested rather than assumed.

기존 기업의 저주

Why do incumbents so often miss radical innovations? A radical product innovation is “a new product that incorporates a substantially different core technology and provides substantially higher customer benefits relative to previous products in the industry” [@chandy1998]. @chandy2000 identify several reasons incumbents resist them. Perceived incentives run through prospect theory: incumbents stand to lose from cannibalizing their position while entrants stand to gain, so the two evaluate the same gamble differently. An organizational filter channels resources toward proven, revenue-generating tasks, and organizational routines make repetitive tasks efficient at the cost of flexibility. Incumbents do hold offsetting opportunities—market capabilities such as customer knowledge, an established franchise, and market power—and, when large, financial and technical capabilities. Because size and incumbency are positively correlated, the (bureaucratic) inertia theory predicts that radical ideas struggle to pass through a large firm’s filtering and screening, absent incentives to push them; yet large firms also command the resources to commercialize radical innovation.

The empirical record overturns the simple inertia story. Using a four-year historical analysis (one author and nine assistants) of consumer durables and office products with high unit sales, with radical innovations identified by significance within each category and rated for radicalness by three experts, @chandy2000 find data for 64 of 93 innovations. The categorical patterns show that large firms are more likely to be incumbents, that small firms were the more radical innovators before World War II while large firms have become the more radical innovators recently, and that U.S. innovators have historically come from non-incumbents and smaller firms but recently from large firms. The multivariate analysis confirms a reversal: historically larger organizations introduced fewer radical innovations, but in recent years the tendency is the opposite, and recent U.S. firms have produced more radical innovations than non-U.S. firms—differences the authors attribute to institutions and culture. Further analysis on the relevant population shows that, relative to their share of all firms, large firms account for a disproportionately high share of radical innovations, and that although incumbents are far outnumbered by non-incumbents in any product class, incumbents still account for about half of radical innovations—raising the question of whether incumbents can also be early entrants.

국제적 및 글로벌 도약

Takeoff is not culturally invariant. @tellis2003 study 137 products across 10 categories in 16 countries with a parametric hazard model and find that European takeoff (about six years after introduction) differs from the U.S. pattern, that time-to-takeoff varies by country and category, and that—perhaps surprisingly—there is little evidence that culture and economic factors explain inter-country differences in time-to-takeoff, though countries lower in uncertainty avoidance and higher in education adopt faster. The practical recommendation is a waterfall (sequential) rather than sprinkler strategy for international rollout. @chandrasekaran2008, studying 16 products in 31 countries with a parametric hazard model, report that the developed–developing economic distinction, product type (work versus fun), cultural clusters, and calendar time all affect takeoff time—and that takeoff times have shortened over historical time. The contrast with @tellis2003 on the role of economic factors is a live tension in the literature. @sood2011 develop methods to predict takeoff, and @zhang2016 study restaurant survival using Yelp data—a hazard-modeling application to firm-level survival rather than category takeoff.

These takeoff studies sit within a broader stocktaking of innovation research. @hauser2006 organize the field into five streams: consumer response to innovation, organizations and innovation, market entry strategies, prescriptive techniques for product-development processes, and defense against market entry.

자기잠식과 파괴 상황에서의 생존

When a successive technology arrives, both incumbents and entrants face a dilemma: the incumbent must decide whether to invest in the new technology, the old, or both, while the entrant must decide whether to target a niche or the mass market. The resolution turns on the relationship between the new and old technologies—a high rate of disengagement (cannibalization) versus a low rate (coexistence). @Chandrasekaran_2020, whose paper was famously rejected five times before publication, model leapfrogging, cannibalization, and survival during disruptive technological change. Disruption occurs when the incumbent focuses on the old technology to the exclusion of the new; cannibalization is the extent to which the successive technology eats into the real or potential sales (or penetration) of the old technology through substitution, captured by a rate of disengagement \(F_{12}\) that admits partial substitution. The adopters of a successive technology partition into leapfroggers (who adopt the new but would never have adopted the old), switchers (who adopted the old and switch once the new arrives), opportunists (who waited for the old but end up with the new), and dual users (who use both).

Building on @norton1987, the penetration of the two technologies is \[ S_1(t) = m_1 F_1(t)\big(1 - F_{12}(t - \tau_2 + 1)\big), \tag{198.21}\] \[ S_2(t) = F_2(t - \tau_2 + 1)\big(m_2 + m_1 F_1(t)\big), \tag{198.22}\] where \(S_i(t)\) is the penetration of technology \(i\) in period \(t\), \(m_1\) is the long-run potential of technology 1, \(m_1 + m_2\) the long-run potential of technology 2, and \(\tau_2\) the introduction time of technology 2. Each fraction takes the Bass form, \[ F_g(t) = \frac{p_g\big(1 - e^{-(p_g + q_g)t}\big)}{p_g + q_g\,e^{-(p_g + q_g)t}}, \qquad g \in \{1, 2\}, \tag{198.23}\] with technology-specific innovation and imitation coefficients \(p_g, q_g\) and separate disengagement coefficients \(p_{12}, q_{12}\) governing the rate \(F_{12}\) at which technology-1 customers abandon it for technology 2. The model’s contributions are to distinguish the adoption rate of technology 2 from the disengagement rate of technology 1 (\(F_2 \neq F_{12}\)), to allow \(p\) and \(q\) to vary across technologies, and to give \(F_{12}\) the same functional form as \(F_1\) and \(F_2\)—a choice that fits the data, reduces to prior models, and applies to both generational and technological diffusion.

Estimation is by nonlinear least squares, minimizing the joint residual sum of squares across both technologies, \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(s_{i1} - m_1 F_1(t_i)\big(1 - F_{12}(t_i - \tau_2 + 1)\big)\Big)^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(s_{i2} - F_2(t_i - \tau_2 + 1)\big(m_2 + m_1 F_1(t_i)\big)\Big)^2. \tag{198.24}\] The adopter segments decompose the technology-2 sales and the cannibalized technology-1 sales, \[ S_2(t) = L_2(t) + DU_2(t) + SW_2(t) + O_2(t), \tag{198.25}\] \[ S_1(t) = L_1(t) - CAN_2(t) = L_1(t) - \big(SW_2(t) + O_2(t)\big), \tag{198.26}\] where \(L\) denotes leapfroggers, \(DU\) dual users, \(SW\) switchers, \(O\) opportunists, and \(CAN\) cannibalization. Market growth is the sum of leapfroggers and dual users; cannibalization is the sum of switchers and opportunists. The managerial value is in distinguishing growth that adds to total demand from substitution that merely reallocates it.

광고 반응

How consumers respond to advertising is the canonical dynamic-effects problem in marketing. The questions are deceptively simple—does advertising work, and if so when, where, why, and for how long?—and the answers require modeling effects that persist beyond the exposure period. Advertising exposure can produce a short (current) effect, a sleeper effect that emerges with delay, hysteresis (a persistent shift in baseline), a long-run effect, and an instant effect. The empirical challenge is to separate these, which means modeling carryover.

정태적 반응에서 코이익 모형으로

The naive model regresses sales on contemporaneous advertising, \[ S_t = \alpha + \beta A_t + \mu_t, \tag{198.27}\] and fails precisely because it ignores carryover. The natural correction is an infinite geometric distributed lag, \[ S_t = \alpha + \beta A_t + \beta \lambda A_{t-1} + \beta \lambda^2 A_{t-2} + \cdots + \epsilon_t, \tag{198.28}\] a moving average with geometrically declining weights that captures carryover exactly, with \(0 < \lambda < 1\) the decay rate. The Koyck transformation [@koyck1954distributed] makes this estimable: lag Equation 198.28 one period, multiply by \(\lambda\), and subtract, \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda S_{t-1} &= \alpha\lambda + \beta\lambda A_{t-1} + \beta\lambda^2 A_{t-2} + \cdots + \lambda\epsilon_{t-1}, \\ S_t - \lambda S_{t-1} &= \alpha(1 - \lambda) + \beta A_t + (\epsilon_t - \lambda\epsilon_{t-1}), \\ S_t &= \alpha(1-\lambda) + \lambda S_{t-1} + \beta A_t + u_t, \end{aligned} \tag{198.29}\] collapsing an infinite lag into a one-period autoregression that is easy to estimate. The parameters are interpretable: \(\beta\) is the current effect of advertising, \(\lambda\) the carryover or decay rate, \(\beta\lambda/(1-\lambda)\) the carryover effect, \(\beta/(1-\lambda)\) the total effect, and the \(p\%\) duration interval—the time to accumulate fraction \(p\) of the total effect—is \(\log(1-p)/\log\lambda\). Adding a lagged advertising term, \[ S_t = \alpha + \lambda S_{t-1} + \beta A_t + \beta_1 A_{t-1} + \mu_t, \tag{198.30}\] separates inertia from advertising carryover, disentangles decay across regressors, and identifies the shape of decay.

@clarke1976 exposes the model’s central vulnerability, aggregation bias: the larger the data interval, the larger the estimated \(\lambda\), the larger the estimated carryover, and the longer the estimated duration of advertising effects. The once-conventional remedy—match the data interval to the interpurchase time—was overturned by @tellis2006, who shows the optimal interval is the unit exposure time: the smallest interval within which advertising occurs only once and at the same time each period.

자기회귀 분포시차와 그 한계

Generalizing the Koyck model yields the autoregressive distributed-lag (ADL) model—a precursor to vector autoregression— \[ S_t = \alpha + \lambda_1 S_{t-1} + \lambda_2 S_{t-2} + \cdots + \beta_0 A_t + \beta_1 A_{t-1} + \cdots + \mu_t, \tag{198.31}\] which accommodates a rich variety of decay shapes: the \(\beta\) coefficients govern the number and position of “bumps” in the response, while the \(\lambda\) coefficients govern the speed of decay. Its costs are also instructive. Aggregate, population-level data cannot identify exposure, aggregate time cannot identify the treated period, advertising budgets are set on expected sales (reverse causality), and the lagged regressors are multicollinear. These limits motivate the two major advances in advertising-response modeling: moving to disaggregate data—individual household or consumer, by day or hour, moment to moment, and in exposures rather than dollars—and moving to quasi-experiments such as difference-in-differences and synthetic control.

직접반응 광고와 전달함수

@tellis2000 study television advertising for a service whose response is a referral—“a call by a customer for the firm’s service.” The theory of message repetition posits a current effect on behavior, a carryover effect on behavior, and a non-behavioral effect on attitude and memory; the research questions ask how advertising affects referrals given current brand equity—through placement, creative, time period, and ad age and repetition—and whether its marginal benefit exceeds its marginal cost. The model regresses referrals on their own lags and on lagged advertising, \[ R_t = \alpha + \gamma_1 R_{t-1} + \gamma_2 R_{t-2} + \gamma_3 R_{t-3} + \beta_0 A_t + \beta_1 A_{t-1} + \beta_2 A_{t-2} + \cdots + \epsilon_t, \tag{198.32}\] with controls for opening hours and time of day. The lagged dependent variables serve two purposes: algebraically, without them the independent-variable lag would be infinite; intuitively, they separate advertising carryover from inertia.

The estimation is a transfer-function (Box–Jenkins) analysis. Autocorrelation and partial-autocorrelation functions reveal hourly and weekly temporal patterns; the lag structure settles on three lags of the dependent and four of advertising. Writing the model with stationary \(R_t\) and \(A_t\), \[ R_t = \alpha + v(\mathbf{B}) A_t + N_t, \tag{198.33}\] where \(v(\mathbf{B}) = C\,w(\mathbf{B})\mathbf{B}^{b}/\delta(\mathbf{B})\) is the transfer function of advertising on referrals and \(N_t = [\theta(\mathbf{B})/\phi(\mathbf{B})] (1-\mathbf{B})^{d} a_t\) with \(a_t \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\) models the noise. The total effect of advertising is the sum of advertising coefficients divided by one minus the sum of lagged-referral coefficients, \[ \text{Total Effect} = \frac{\sum_{l=0}^{n} \beta_l}{1 - \sum_{j=1}^{p} \lambda_j}, \tag{198.34}\] and the partial advertising effect at each lag is the recursion \[ TA_{t-l} = \beta_l A_{t-l} + \sum_{j=0}^{l} \lambda_j\,TA_{t-l+j}. \tag{198.35}\] The results are managerially crisp: advertising effects dissipate after about eight hours, effectiveness varies by station, and creatives differ.

최적 자료 간격

@tellis2006 is a seminal treatment of a question that lurks beneath every dynamic advertising model: at what temporal granularity should the data be recorded? The counterintuitive answer is that too disaggregate does not cause bias—the optimal interval is the unit exposure time, not the interpurchase time—and that the true parameters depend on the unit exposure time rather than on any assumed advertising process. The result generalizes beyond advertising; the same logic governs the optimal interval for estimating, say, an announcement’s effect on stock performance. Table 198.3 fixes the vocabulary.

The optimal interval balances storage cost against estimator unbiasedness. At the true micro-data interval, the Koyck model is \[ s_t = \mu + \beta a_t + \beta\lambda a_{t-1} + \beta\lambda^2 a_{t-2} + \cdots + \epsilon_t, \qquad \epsilon_t \sim N(0, \sigma^2_\epsilon), \tag{198.36}\] with \(\beta\) the current effect, \(\beta/(1-\lambda)\) the carryover, and \(\lambda\) determining the duration interval. Applying the Koyck transformation (multiplying by \(1 - \lambda L\) for lag operator \(L\), \(L^k y_t = y_{t-k}\)), \[ s_t = \lambda s_{t-1} + \beta a_t + \epsilon_t - \lambda \epsilon_{t-1}. \tag{198.37}\] Aggregating \(K\) consecutive periods sampled at the current period defines \[ S_T = (1 + L + L^2 + \cdots + L^{K-1}) s_t, \tag{198.38}\] and analogously \(A_T\), \(\epsilon_T\), and \(S_{T-1} = (1 + L + \cdots + L^{K-1}) s_{t-K}\). The true aggregate form of the micromodel is \[ \begin{aligned} S_T = {}& \lambda^{K} S_{T-1} + \beta A_T \\ & + \beta\lambda\,(1 + \lambda L + \cdots + \lambda^{K-1} L^{K-1})(1 + L + \cdots + L^{K-1}) a_{t-1} + \epsilon_T - \lambda^{K} \epsilon_{T-1}. \end{aligned} \tag{198.39}\] The bias arises because aggregation loses the cross term, that is, \[ A_{T-1} \neq (1 + \lambda L + \cdots + \lambda^{K-1} L^{K-1})(1 + L + \cdots + L^{K-1}) a_{t-1}. \tag{198.40}\] With the optimal interval—one exposure pulse per interval—the carryover effect is recovered as \((\beta_1 + \beta_2)/(1 - \lambda^{K})\), the true duration interval as \(\sqrt[K]{\hat{\lambda}^{K}}\), and the current effect as \(\beta\); with data more disaggregate than the optimal interval, the formulas adjust to recover the same true effects.

펄싱과 광고 회피

@teixeira2010 study how advertising’s temporal pattern within a commercial affects consumers’ tendency to avoid it. Using eye-tracking data on 31 commercials viewed by roughly 2,000 participants, estimated with a probit model via MCMC, they develop a new metric for attention dispersion from gaze data. The optimization problem—minimize avoidance subject to a target level of brand activity—has pulsing as its solution: concentrating brand presence in bursts reduces avoidance relative to a constant presence.

광고 탄력성: 메타분석

Synthesizing 56 studies spanning 1960–2008, @sethuraman2011 estimate an average short-term advertising elasticity of about 0.12 and a long-term elasticity of about 0.24, with a documented decline in advertising elasticity over historical time. Elasticity is higher for durable than nondurable goods, in the early than the mature life-cycle stage, with yearly than quarterly data, and when advertising is measured in gross rating points rather than monetary terms. These benchmarks discipline any single study’s estimate.

텔레비전, 온라인 행동 및 준실험

The disaggregate-data and quasi-experimental advances are vividly illustrated by studies linking television advertising to online behavior. @liaukonyte2015 merge $3.4 billion of advertising spending by 20 brands with second-by-second traffic and transaction data for 1,224 commercials, using human coders for impression merging. Their difference-in-differences design compares two-minute pre/post windows—close to a regression-discontinuity logic—and finds that action-focused content raises direct website traffic and sales conditional on a visit; information- and emotion-focused content reduces traffic but raises purchases, with a positive net sales effect for most brands; and imagery-focused content decreases direct traffic. The behavioral model is sequential: after the ad, the consumer first decides whether to visit the website, then whether to buy. The data combine comScore Media Metrix online traffic (direct traffic, search-engine referrals, transaction counts) with Kantar Media ad data. The identification argument against endogeneity is that brands cannot control the exact second their ad airs—it is placed within a 15-minute window while the design examines a 4-minute window—and for the two-hour analysis a difference-in-differences design uses the largest non-advertising brand within each category as a control.

@tirunillai2017 examine television advertising’s effect on online chatter using synthetic control. The raw metrics come from reviews (Amazon, Epinions, CNET, Twitter, YouTube, Facebook—volume, valence, and entropy-based polarity) and from blogs (via Spinn3r—volume, the in-degree of the brand website, the in-degree of blog posts, and the volume of blogs gaining or losing rank). A dynamic factor model extracts latent dimensions, \[ Y_t = \boldsymbol{\xi} f_t + \epsilon_t, \qquad f_t = \boldsymbol{\Psi} f_{t-1} + \eta_t, \tag{198.41}\] where \(Y_t\) is the raw vector of review and blog measures, \(f_t\) the latent factors, \(\boldsymbol{\xi}\) the loadings, \(\epsilon_t\) idiosyncratic error, and \(\eta_t\) white noise with \(\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_t \eta'_{t-k}] = 0\). The factors resolve into content-based dimensions—popularity (loading on review and blog volume) and negativity (loading on valence and polarity)—and information-spread dimensions— visibility (blog volume and brand-website in-degree) and virality (blogs gaining rank and blog in-degree). Television advertising causally produces a short positive effect on chatter, larger on information spread than on content, and reduces negativity in the short run—working by stimulating conversation, triggering brand recall, framing the interpretation of experience favorably, and lending credibility that refutes negatives. The empirical setting is a “Let’s Do Amazing” campaign with a 70-day pre-window and 20-day post-window (the asymmetric window is not strongly justified), the synthetic brand is constructed to net out within-industry spillover (which the authors argue is absent), YouTube viewership is controlled with Visible Measures and TV viewership with Nielsen and other ratings, and a vector-autoregression complements the synthetic-control design to examine short- and long-run dynamics.

기업가치에 대한 마케팅 수익

The terminal link in the dynamic chain runs from marketing actions, through consumer and competitive response, to the firm’s financial value. Establishing that link requires the apparatus of event analysis and a clear-eyed view of which designs support causal claims about returns.

인과추론의 사다리

It helps to order the available designs by the rigor of causal inference they support. In decreasing order: lab experiment, field experiment, natural experiment, instrumental variables, Granger causality (improved by exogenous shocks), time-series regression (likewise improved by shocks), and cross-sectional regression. The same ordering appears as a ladder of field tests of causality—from bare correlation, to multiple regression that controls for plausible alternative causes, to time-series models using current and past values (Koyck, ADL, ARIMA), to first differences (effects of changes), to lags of first differences in the @arellano1991 spirit, to Granger causality using only past values of the independent variables while controlling for past values of the dependent variable (preferably a VAR in differences), to intervention or event analysis, to natural experiments, and finally to randomized controlled trials. Figure 198.2 depicts the ascent.

The financial logic rests on the efficient-market idealization in which a stock price \(P_t\) follows a random walk, so that the return \(P_t - P_{t-1}\) is white noise and any abnormal return signals new information. A typical two-stage panel design samples similar firms \(j\), identifies each firm’s similar events, estimates the abnormal returns \(e_{jt}\) associated with each event in a first stage (using WRDS data), and in a second stage pools those abnormal returns to estimate the factors that shift their distribution. The strength of an event analysis increases with a clearly defined event, a narrow treatment window, the removal of confounding events, a long pre-event baseline, a large and diverse set of firms and treatment contexts, and the extraction of known predictors’ effects—because it simulates a natural experiment around a natural or artificial shock. Natural experiments themselves come in flavors: treated-versus-untreated comparisons, before-versus-after comparisons, difference-in-differences, and synthetic control; pre-period controls range from a single prior period, to a baseline of prior periods, to a synthetic control, to a function of known factors (the Fama–French factors), to crossover designs in which the treated unit later becomes the control. Table 198.4 lists the archival sources that make such designs feasible in marketing.

고객만족과 주식수익률

That customer satisfaction affects firm economic performance is long understood; its relationship to stock performance is the open question @fornell2006 address, under the hypothesis that the market does not impound satisfaction information immediately (a departure from strict efficiency). Four channels link satisfaction to firm value: acceleration of cash flows (faster buyer response), increases in cash flows (repeat business at low marginal cost), reduction in cash-flow risk, and an increase in the residual value of the business. Combining Compustat with the American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI), a correlational regression relates market value to book value, book-value liabilities, and the satisfaction index, \[ \ln(\text{Market value}) = \alpha + \beta_1 \ln(\text{Book value}) + \beta_2 \ln(\text{Book-value liability}) + \beta_3 \ln(\text{ACSI}) + \varepsilon, \tag{198.42}\] and finds a positive association. Investors do not always reward higher satisfaction, however—because the firm may be giving away consumer surplus, may already lead its competitors, may face a satisfaction–productivity trade-off, because causality may run in reverse, or because the timing of satisfaction measurement complicates inference.

The event study estimates abnormal returns with the market model, \[ AR_{jt} = R_{jt} - (\alpha_j + \beta_j R_{mt}), \tag{198.43}\] for firm \(j\) on day \(t\), with an estimation period of 255 days ending 46 days before the event [@mcwilliams1997a], a one-day event window on the Wall Street Journal’s ACSI publication date, and a five-day pre/post screen to rule out confounds such as mergers, spin-offs, splits, executive changes, layoffs, restructurings, earnings, and lawsuits. The event study finds no evidence that ACSI announcements move cumulative abnormal returns. The complementary portfolio study, comparing a hypothetical to a real-world portfolio, finds that customer satisfaction does help portfolios earn higher returns in both up and down markets—a discrepancy between the announcement-level and portfolio-level findings that motivated much subsequent work.

That subsequent work includes a pointed reassessment. @jacobson2009 dispute the claim of systematic mispricing of satisfaction [@fornell2006; @aksoy2008], arguing the anomaly stems from a small group of satisfaction leaders in the computer and internet sectors—a sampling bias—consistent with @osullivan2009; the companion @jacobson2009a develops the argument further.

마케팅, 혁신 및 기업가치

Marketing investments do not translate into firm value readily, in part because they are typically intangible—brand equity, customer equity, customer satisfaction, R&D, product quality, and specific marketing-mix actions—and in part because markets are not perfectly efficient, so that intangible-intensive firms are often undervalued [@lev1989]. @srinivasan2009 review the modeling of the marketing–value link. The workhorse is a factor model in which excess returns load on a market factor (excess return on a broad portfolio), a size factor (large minus small caps), a value factor (high minus low book-to-market), and a momentum factor; the metrics of interest are top-line (revenue) and bottom-line (earnings) surprises, and even a four-factor model can suffer omitted-variable bias. Measuring marketing’s contribution to value requires isolating book value (via Tobin’s \(q\)) and accommodating the random-walk behavior of prices (the first difference of log price). Table 198.5, adapted from the review, contrasts the principal approaches; Figure 198.3 sketches the flow from marketing actions through returns and risk to firm value.

The four-factor (Carhart) model that underlies most of these designs is \[ R_{it} - R_{rf,t} = \alpha_i + \beta_i (R_{mt} - R_{rf,t}) + s_i\,SMB_t + h_i\,HML_t + u_i\,UMD_t + \epsilon_{it}, \tag{198.44}\] where \(R_{it}\) is firm \(i\)’s return, \(R_{rf,t}\) the risk-free rate, \(R_{mt} - R_{rf,t}\) the market factor, \(SMB_t\) the size factor (small minus big), \(HML_t\) the value factor (high minus low book-to-market), and \(UMD_t\) the momentum factor (up minus down). A significant \(\alpha_i\) after conditioning on the four factors is the abnormal performance attributed to the marketing variable of interest.

@sood2009a apply the event-study apparatus to innovation, distinguishing three activity types—initiation (alliances, funding, expansions), development (prototypes, patents), and commercialization (product launches, awards)—and find that innovation’s effect on stock prices is underestimated when distinct events are aggregated. The total market return to an innovation project is about $643 million, against roughly $49 million for an average single event; positive events raise returns across all three stages, negative events lower returns only in development and commercialization, and the absolute return is larger for negative than positive announcements. @borah2014 extend this to the firm’s make–buy–ally choice for new technologies, modeling returns, the investment choice (a multinomial logit over make, buy, and ally at initiation), and payoffs across the initiation, development, and commercialization phases—the last spanning launch, initial shipments, new applications and markets, and awards.

온라인 담론과 주가 성과

@tirunillai2012 ask how user-generated content (UGC) relates to stock performance: the direction of causality, which UGC metric best relates to performance, and the dynamics of wear-in, wear-out, and duration. Over four years, six markets, and 15 firms—chosen because reviews relate to sales, the firms are public, no mergers occurred, and the markets are representative—they measure UGC as product ratings, chatter volume, and positive and negative valence from Amazon, Epinions, and Yahoo! Shopping (consumer reviews preferred to expert reviews for the wisdom of crowds, and to blogs and forums for a higher signal-to-noise ratio). Stock performance is measured as abnormal returns and idiosyncratic risk from a Fama–French three-factor plus Carhart momentum model, and trading volume as daily turnover. The asymmetry hypotheses—losses loom larger than gains, investors discount firm-influenced positive information—motivate an asymmetric specification.

Abnormal returns follow the four-factor model with an EGARCH variance to capture volatility asymmetry, \[ R_{i,t} - R_{f,t} = \alpha_i + \beta_{i,MKT}(R_{MKT,t} - R_{f,t}) + \beta_{i,SMB} SMB_t + \beta_{i,HML} HML_t + \beta_{i,MOM} MOM_t + \epsilon_{i,t}, \tag{198.45}\] with \(\epsilon_{i,t} \sim N(0, \sigma_{i,t})\) and \[ \ln(\sigma^2_{i,t}) = a_i + \sum_{j=1}^{p} b_{i,j}\ln(\sigma^2_{i,t-j}) + \sum_{k=1}^{q} c_{i,k}\Big\{\Theta\Big(\frac{\epsilon_{i,t-k}}{\sigma_{i,t-k}}\Big) + \Gamma\Big(\Big|\frac{\epsilon_{i,t-k}}{\sigma_{i,t-k}}\Big| - \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{\pi}}\Big)\Big\}. \tag{198.46}\] Controls include analysts’ forecasts (IBES), television advertising (TNS), media citations (LexisNexis above 60% relevance and Factiva), and new-product announcements (LexisNexis and Factiva, following @sood2009). The dynamic analysis uses a vector autoregression, chosen over event studies because it handles continuous events, captures immediate and lagged effects, recovers carryover via the generalized impulse response function, and controls for trends, seasonality, nonstationarity, serial correlation, and reverse causality [@luo2009quantifying]. The procedure tests stationarity (augmented Dickey–Fuller and KPSS) and cointegration (Johansen’s procedure [@johansen1992determination]), tests Granger causality, estimates carryover via impulse responses (insensitive to the variables’ causal ordering), and apportions explained variance via forecast-error variance decomposition. The findings: chatter volume raises abnormal returns and trading volume (by Granger tests); positive UGC moves neither returns nor idiosyncratic risk; negative UGC lowers returns with a short wear-in and long wear-out and raises idiosyncratic risk; the volume–negativity interaction raises trading volume; and offline advertising raises chatter volume while reducing negative chatter.

실행 예시: 사건연구

To make the machinery concrete and reproducible, the following simulation generates returns for a treated firm and a market index, estimates the market model (Equation 198.43) over a pre-event window, and computes the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around a simulated marketing event with a true one-day impact. ?fig-event-study plots the abnormal returns and the accumulating CAR around the event.

#| label: fig-event-study
#| fig-cap: "Simulated event study. Top: daily abnormal returns around the event (day 0), with the true positive shock visible. Bottom: cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over the event window."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
set.seed(37)

n_est   <- 250            # estimation-window length (days)
n_event <- 21             # event window: -10 .. +10
alpha_t <- 0.0002         # true firm alpha
beta_t  <- 1.1            # true firm beta
shock   <- 0.03           # true abnormal return on event day (day 0)

# Market returns: white noise around a small drift (random-walk prices)
r_mkt <- rnorm(n_est + n_event, mean = 0.0003, sd = 0.010)

# Firm returns generated by the market model plus idiosyncratic noise
eps   <- rnorm(n_est + n_event, mean = 0, sd = 0.012)
r_firm <- alpha_t + beta_t * r_mkt + eps

# Inject the event shock on the event day (last day of the window)
event_day <- n_est + 11          # index of day 0 within the window
r_firm[event_day] <- r_firm[event_day] + shock

# Estimate the market model on the estimation window only
est_idx <- seq_len(n_est)
fit <- lm(r_firm[est_idx] ~ r_mkt[est_idx])

# Abnormal returns over the event window
evt_idx <- (n_est + 1):(n_est + n_event)
ar <- r_firm[evt_idx] - (coef(fit)[1] + coef(fit)[2] * r_mkt[evt_idx])
car <- cumsum(ar)
rel_day <- -10:10

op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
plot(rel_day, ar, type = "h", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Event day", ylab = "Abnormal return",
     main = "Abnormal returns around the event")
abline(h = 0, col = "grey60"); abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "red")
plot(rel_day, car, type = "b", pch = 16,
     xlab = "Event day", ylab = "Cumulative abnormal return",
     main = "CAR over the event window")
abline(h = 0, col = "grey60"); abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "red")
par(op)

round(c(alpha_hat = coef(fit)[1], beta_hat = coef(fit)[2],
        CAR_event_window = tail(car, 1)), 4)

The estimated \(\hat\alpha\) and \(\hat\beta\) recover the data-generating values, and the CAR steps up at day 0 by approximately the injected shock—exactly the abnormal return an event study is designed to detect. The design’s credibility hinges on the assumptions catalogued above: a clean event date, a confound-free window, and a market model that adequately describes normal returns.

창의성과 아이디어 선별

Social media reshapes the economics of innovation along two axes: it makes the wisdom of the crowds available for idea generation and evaluation, and it makes advertising nearly free. Both invite a strategic-dynamic treatment of how ideas are produced, screened, and rewarded over time.

@bayus2013 study crowdsourced ideation over time at Dell’s IdeaStorm community and find a striking dynamic: serial ideators are more likely than others to produce a single implemented idea, but they do not repeat that success. The mechanism is a fixation effect—an unconscious reuse of one’s own prior ideas, akin to cryptomnesia or unconscious plagiarism [@marsh1995; @marsh1999]—whose negative effect on subsequent success is mitigated for ideators with more diverse commenting activity. As the first study of idea crowdsourcing over time, with a well-motivated theory and strong descriptive analysis, its principal limitation is a model that does not accommodate rare events.

@toubia2017 formalize creativity as a balance between novelty and familiarity, invoking a “beauty in averageness” effect and building an automated reader to identify promising ideas. Drawing on the Geneplore framework, they define novelty as “the association of word stems that do not appear frequently together in text related to the topic” and familiarity as “the association of word stems that appear frequently together,” and measure both with semantic-network co-word analysis over word-stem combinations rather than individual words. An idea is “a document made of words that attempts to add value given a particular idea-generation topic.” Edge weights use the Jaccard index; a baseline semantic network is built from pre-test ideas and top Google results (the latter possibly biased toward high-quality content); control variables follow @barrat2007 (node frequencies, clustering coefficients, and network-size features). The distance between an idea’s edge-weight distribution and a prototypical distribution is measured by the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic (or, alternatively, Kullback–Leibler divergence), with an information-retrieval vector-space representation as an alternative to edge-weight distributions. Ideas are evaluated manually on creativity, purchase interest, predicted popularity, and writing quality. The method’s strength is measuring a complex, qualitative construct robustly across measures, ideas, evaluators, and baseline networks, with a tight theory–method link; its weakness is sensitivity to the choice of representation—under some representations the results do not hold—and to the specification of the baseline network.

@wei2021 bring machine learning to crowdfunding creativity, motivated by combinatorial theory and the need to measure novelty, over- and under-shooting of funding goals, and styles of imitation. Across 98,058 Kickstarter projects (2009–2017, in Film & Video, Music, and Publishing, English only), they measure semantic similarity with word2vec at the word level and Word Mover’s Distance at the document level, constructing a similarity network whose link strength \[ w_{ij} = \delta^{|t_i - t_j|} \times L(\gamma_0 - \gamma_1 d_{ij}) \tag{198.47}\] increases with similarity and decreases with the time lag between projects, where \(0 < \delta \le 1\) is a decay factor, \(d_{ij}\) the Word Mover’s Distance, and \(L\) the logistic function. Funding performance is modeled with logistic regression (success) and linear regression (amount raised). The network-based metrics include the amount of prior similarity, the prior success rate (a weighted average over similar projects), the prior success residual, goal overshoot (log difference from similar projects’ average goal), and atypicality (the proportion of isolated nodes in a project’s unweighted subnetwork at a 0.5 cutoff). Information is weighted as \[ I_i \equiv \log\!\Big(1 + \sum_{j:\,T_j < t_i} w_{ij}\Big), \tag{198.48}\] a specification chosen because it is zero when no prior similarity exists and embeds a Bayesian diminishing return to additional signals. The findings: the average success of prior similar projects predicts current funding performance; high novelty (low similarity to all priors) helps, but the best projects balance novelty with apparent familiarity; goals should be set close to similar projects’ goals (within about \(\pm 10\%\)); and atypicality (borrowing from another stream) has an inverted-U relation with funding performance. The results are robust to an unweighted network thresholded on similarity.

Whether AI can do ideation—screening rather than generating—has been studied with three model families: word colocation, content atypicality, and inspiration redundancy, predicted with LASSO, random forests, and RuleFit. Two component findings anchor this work: @berger2018 show that ideas score better when they are atypical relative to others in the same contest, and @stephen2016 show that ideators with more diverse network backgrounds generate less redundant, better ideas.

품질

품질 is a fundamental construct across policy, economics, consumer behavior, and marketing strategy. The classic definition is an attribute on which all (or most) consumers prefer more to less—speed, reliability, durability, power [@tellis1987]—and the existence of a market for quality [@klein1981] explains why quality commands a premium. The measurement problem is that quality is multidimensional, so any composite depends on the choice of dimensions and weights.

Historically, objective quality was measured by Consumer Reports (from 1935 until about 2010): blind experiments evaluated by experts. The weighting problem is real but tractable. @kopalle1992 show that ranking products on quality is not too noisy even when the weights are uncorrelated, provided the quality attributes are positively correlated; @tellis2007 show that published expert quality ratings are good indicators of quality; and @tirunillai2014a show that the wisdom of crowds, mined from reviews, recovers quality as well.

@tellis2009 study network effects and quality in high technology and find evidence for market efficiency, defined as the best-quality brand holding the largest market share. Both quality and network effects drive market-share flows—network effects more than quality—where a network effect is “the increase in a consumer’s utility from a product when the number of other users of that product increases,” and quality is “a composite of a brand’s attributes, on each of which all consumers prefer more to less” (reliability, performance, convenience). 품질 appears to be the market’s driving force across market share, return on investment, price premia, advertising, perceived quality, and stock-market return, in the personal-computer category using International Data Corporation and Dataquest data.

@golder2012 provide an integrative framework that decomposes quality into three processes. The quality-production process focuses on firms—attribute design, process design, resource inputs, and production control. The quality-experience process focuses on customers, recognizing that what a firm delivers and what a customer perceives (relative to expectation) can differ, mediated by the customer’s measurement knowledge, motivation, and emotions, so that experienced attribute quality diverges from delivered attribute quality. The quality-evaluation process converts perceived attributes into an aggregated judgment based on transactional and global assessments, shaped by customer expertise and by three kinds of expectation: “will,” “ideal,” and “should.” 품질 is defined as “a set of three distinct states of an offering’s attributes’ relative performance generated while producing, experiencing, and evaluating the offering.” Table 198.6 gives the accompanying typology of attributes along customer-preference homogeneity and measurement ambiguity.

@tirunillai2014a mine quality from consumer reviews with unsupervised latent Dirichlet allocation over 350,000 reviews from @tirunillai2012, recovering quality dimensions that allow marketers to track value over time and to map competitive brand positions dynamically. The structure of those dimensions differs by market type, as Table 198.7 summarizes.

Finally, quality and reputation spill across brands. @borah2016 study spillover effects in social media, documenting a perverse halo—negative spillover in which negative chatter about one nameplate raises negative chatter about another, affecting both sales and stock performance. The effect depends on similarity in market share (a dominant brand’s spillover is stronger) and on shared country of origin (similar origins suffer more), and apology advertising harms both the recalled brand and its rivals; online chatter amplifies the negative sales effect of recalls roughly 4.5-fold. The mechanism is accessibility–diagnosticity [@feldman1988]: one brand’s perceptions inform inferences about a similar brand. In the automobile context (January 2009–April 2010, covering Toyota’s acceleration crisis), the endogenous variables include negative online chatter, media citations (LexisNexis at 60% relevance, as in @tirunillai2012), ABC News coverage, negative-event indicators, advertising types (including apology ads), and key developments from Capital IQ; the exogenous variables include recall units and new-product introductions, both shown by Granger tests to be plausibly exogenous. A VARX model estimates Granger causality and long-run effects via impulse response functions—robust to nonstationarity, spurious causality, endogeneity, serial correlation, and reverse causality. The perverse halo is confirmed: stronger across same-country and from dominant to less-dominant brands, with a one-day wear-in and six-day wear-out; apology ads increase concern; concern about a nameplate significantly depresses both its own and its rival’s sales (explaining more of the focal nameplate’s sales variance, by forecast-error variance decomposition); and rising concern depresses Toyota’s stock performance to a trough on the fourth day, with mixed effects on rivals owing to country-of-origin moderation.

핵심 요점

Three threads run through this chapter. First, the object of inference is a trajectory, not a point: diffusion curves, advertising decay, and abnormal-return paths are all dynamic, and the models that fit them—Bass and its generalizations, Koyck and the ADL/VAR family, hazard models, and event studies—are organized by the nature of the series rather than by topic. Second, identification is the binding constraint: the Bass model is fragile before its turning points, proportional-hazards estimates rest on a testable proportionality assumption, distributed-lag models suffer aggregation bias that the unit-exposure-time result of @tellis2006 resolves, and event-study causality lives or dies by the cleanliness of the event window and the counterfactual. Third, the strategic payoff is real: knowing whether a product will take off, whether a new technology cannibalizes or coexists, how long advertising lasts, and what a marketing event is worth to shareholders are precisely the questions on which entry, investment, and budgeting decisions turn. The empirical record repeatedly corrects naive intuition—pioneers mostly fail, larger firms have become the radical innovators, emotion beats information in advertising, and negative chatter moves markets while positive chatter does not—and each correction is only as credible as the design that produced it.

추가 읽을거리

For the foundations of diffusion modeling, @Bass_1969 and the comprehensive review of @chandrasekaran2007 are the indispensable starting points, with @golder1997 and @tellis2003 for the turning-point literature. For advertising dynamics, @koyck1954distributed, @clarke1976, and the optimal-interval result of @tellis2006 form a natural sequence, complemented by the meta-analytic benchmarks of @sethuraman2011. For the marketing–finance interface, @srinivasan2009 surveys the modeling landscape, and @tirunillai2012 and @borah2016 illustrate the vector-autoregressive treatment of online chatter and firm value. The market-entry and innovation strategy literatures are reviewed in @hauser2006, with 1 and @chandy2000 as the seminal empirical correctives to received wisdom.

선택 모형과 수요 추정 세미나

선택 모형(choice modeling)과 수요 추정(demand estimation)은 계량 마케팅 및 마케팅이 차용한 산업조직론 전통의 실증적 핵심이다. 이 분야는 하나의 강력한 아이디어에 기반한다. 즉, 관찰된 구매는 대안 간의 잠재적 효용 극대화 비교에서 비롯된 실현된 결과이며, 따라서 개인이 선택하는 방식에 대한 모형을 시장이 수요하는 방식에 대한 모형으로 집계할 수 있다는 것이다. 본 세미나는 확률효용(random-utility) 미시적 기초에서 출발하여 비집계 패널 데이터를 활용한 개인 선택의 추정을 거쳐, 시장 수준 데이터로부터 집계 수요 체계를 복원하고, 나아가 이러한 수요 체계가 답하기 위해 구축된 반사실적(counterfactual) 질문 및 후생(welfare) 분석에 이르는 전 과정을 다룬다. 본 세미나는 추정량을 완전하게 전개하는 본서의 기술적 장들, 즉 선택 및 베이지안 방법론 챕터(이산 선택 및 베이지안 방법론)와 구조 모형 및 산업조직론 내용에 대한 박사과정 리딩 맵 역할을 수행하며, 이는 분석적 모델링 세미나와 해당 방법론 챕터 간의 관계와 동일하다.

이 학문이 중요한 이유는 거의 모든 경영상 및 정책적 질문이 궁극적으로 수요라는 대상에 기초하기 때문이다. 가격 탄력성은 수요의 도함수이고, 기업 결합(합병) 시뮬레이션은 수요의 반사실적 분석이며, 신제품으로 인한 후생 증가는 수요곡선 아래의 적분값이고, 광고나 구색(assortment) 의사결정의 수익률은 수요 반응이다. 상업적으로도 동일한 메커니즘이 차별화된 제품 산업에서 가격 책정 엔진, 구색 최적화, 기업 결합에 대한 규제 심사를 뒷받침한다. 본 세미나의 지적 성과는 학생들로 하여금 이처럼 이질적인 응용 사례들을 하나의 동일한 추정 문제의 변형으로 바라보고, 각 응용 사례가 어떤 가정을 전제하고 있는지를 파악하도록 훈련한다는 점에 있다.

매주 논의를 관통하는 핵심적 긴장은 식별(identification)이다. 선호는 직접 관찰되지 않으며 오직 선택만이 관찰된다. 연구자는 소비자가 직면하는 가격 자체가 연구자가 관찰하지 못하는 수요 변동 요인을 관찰하는 기업에 의해 설정되는 데이터로부터 선호 모수, 특히 가격 민감도를 복원해야 한다. 내생적 가격, 관찰되지 않는 제품 품질, 그리고 제한되지 않은 선호 이질성은 하류의 모든 분석이 의존하는 탄력성 추정치를 오염시킬 위험이 있다. 이 분야의 발전사는 이러한 오염을 해소하기 위해 고안된 도구변수, 통제 함수(control functions), 그리고 분포 가정들의 역사라 할 수 있다. 본 세미나를 마친 학생은 수요 관련 논문을 읽고 가격 계수를 식별하는 변량의 원천, 그 변량을 외생적으로 만드는 가정, 그리고 해당 가정이 정당화하는 반사실적 분석을 즉각 파악할 수 있게 된다. Figure 199.1는 이러한 오염 구조와 세미나에서 다루는 해결책들을 도식화한 것이다.

학기 구성

14주간의 강의는 세 개의 중첩된 단계로 구성된다. 첫 3분의 1(1~4주차)에서는 확률효용 미시적 기초와 비집계 추정량을 다룬다. 즉, McFadden의 조건부 로짓과 Thurstone 및 Luce의 심리학적 기원, 스캐너 패널에 대한 최초의 마케팅 응용, 무관한 대안의 독립성(IIA) 문제와 이를 해결하기 위한 중첩 로짓(nested logit) 및 일반화 극치(GEV) 모형, 그리고 선택 확률에서 선호 이질성을 적분해 냄으로써 IIA 문제를 근본적으로 해소하는 확률계수(random-coefficients) 또는 혼합 로짓(mixed logit) 모형을 학습한다. 중간 3분의 1(5~8주차)에서는 이질성과 집계 문제를 다룬다. 즉, 개인 수준 모수의 위계적 베이지안(hierarchical Bayes) 추정, 컨조인트 및 진술 선호 측정, 그리고 Berry 역변환과 Berry–Levinsohn–Pakes (BLP) 확률계수 수요 모형을 통한 개인 선택에서 집계 수요로의 결정적 전환과 이를 추정하는 실무적 기법을 다룬다.

마지막 3분의 1(9~14주차)에서는 정적 수요 체계를 동적 및 전략적 환경으로 확장한 후 후생 분석으로 귀결된다. 9주차와 10주차에서는 정적·완전정보 벤치마크를 완화하여 소비자의 비축(stockpiling), 내구재 가격 하락에 대한 대기, 전체 구색을 평가하는 대신 내생적 고려군(consideration set) 내에서 탐색하는 행태를 다룬다. 11주차와 12주차는 방법론 중심 모듈로서, 선택 모형의 내생성(통제 함수, 코퓰러, 도구변수)과 풍부한 이질적 모형을 추정 가능하게 만드는 베이지안 및 마르코프 연쇄 몬테카를로(MCMC) 메커니즘을 다룬다. 13주차는 머신러닝의 프론티어인 유연한 수요 예측 및 이질적 처치 효과 추정을 구조적 수요 추정과 접목한다. 14주차는 근본 원리로 돌아가 수요 체계의 존재 이유가 후생 및 반사실적 분석을 계산하는 데 있음을 확인하며, 전체 연구 프로그램을 정당화하는 신제품 및 기업 결합 후생 논문들을 학습한다. Figure 199.2는 14주간의 구성을 3단계 구조로 도식화한 것이다.

리딩 맵은 두 가지 태그를 사용한다. [F] = Foundational(기초 고전)은 선택 및 수요 연구자가 완벽히 숙지해야 할 정전을 나타내며, [R] = Frontier/Recent(최신 프론티어)는 문헌의 발전에 따라 갱신되는 활발한 연구 전선을 나타낸다. 매주 최소 하나 이상의 기초 고전 연구와 최신 연구 또는 방법론적 연구를 짝지어 구성하였다. DOI는 Crossref REST API를 통해 검증된 것을 수록하였으며, 검증 가능한 DOI가 없는 저작(주로 표준 단행본 및 1974년 편집 도서 챕터)은 링크 없이 명시하고 본문에서 이를 표시하였다.

1주차 — 확률효용의 기초

주제. 이후 모든 논의의 미시적 기초가 되는 확률효용모형(RUM): 의사결정자는 연구자가 확률적 오차 항 범위 내에서만 관찰할 수 있는 잠재적 효용을 극대화하며, 이 오차 항의 분포가 선택 확률을 생성한다.

세부 주제. 결정론적 효용 대 확률적 효용; 가법적 오차(additive-error) 설정; 극치(extreme-value) 분포 가정과 로짓의 닫힌 형태(closed form); 확률적 선택의 심리학적 기원.

방법론. 다항/조건부 로짓의 최대우도추정(MLE); 척도(scale) 및 수준(level)에 대한 식별; 로그우도함수와 그 오목성(concavity).

핵심 문헌.

  • McFadden (1974), “Conditional Logit Analysis of Qualitative Choice Behavior,” in Zarembka (ed.), Frontiers in Econometrics, Academic Press — 극치 오차를 갖는 효용 극대화를 로짓 선택 확률과 연결한 기초 논문; Crossref DOI 없음(편집 도서 챕터), 링크 없이 표기. [F]
  • Luce (1959), Individual Choice Behavior: A Theoretical Analysis, Wiley — 로짓이 조작화하는 선택 공리(무관한 대안으로부터의 독립성, IIA); 표준 단행본, DOI 없음. [F]
  • Thurstone (1927), “A Law of Comparative Judgment,” Psychological Review — 전체 전통의 닻이 되는 최초의 확률효용/판별과정(discriminal-process) 아이디어. doi:10.1037/h0070288 — 확률적 선택의 프로빗 형태 기원. [F]

토론 주제. 로짓의 다루기 쉬운 극치 오차 가정은 실질적인 행동적 주장인가, 아니면 이후 IIA 결과를 되돌려야만 하는 수학적 편의에 불과한가?

2주차 — 스캐너 데이터를 활용한 브랜드 선택

주제. RUM의 첫 번째 위대한 마케팅 응용: 동일한 가구가 여러 구매 시점에 걸쳐 반복적으로 선택하는 슈퍼마켓 스캐너 패널로부터 브랜드 선택 확률을 추정.

세부 주제. 충성도(loyalty)와 상태 의존성(state dependence); 브랜드 충성도 및 구매 사건 피드백 변수; 효용 함수 내 마케팅 믹스 공변량(가격, 진열, 판촉 피처); 브랜드 선택을 둘러싼 구매 발생 및 수량 결정.

방법론. 패널 선택 데이터에 대한 조건부 로짓; 지수 평활 충성도 회귀변수 구축; 구매 시점 및 수량과 브랜드 선택의 결합 모델링.

핵심 문헌.

  • Guadagni & Little (1983), “A Logit Model of Brand Choice Calibrated on Scanner Data,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.2.3.203 — 조건부 로짓을 마케팅에 도입하고 충성도 변수 템플릿을 정립한 논문. [F]
  • Gupta (1988), “Impact of Sales Promotions on When, What, and How Much to Buy,” Journal of Marketing Research. doi:10.2307/3172945 — 판촉 반응을 구매 시점, 브랜드 선택, 구매 수량 구성요소로 분해하여 스캐너 선택 연구 프로그램을 단순 브랜드 선택 이상으로 확장. [F]

토론 주제. 충성도 변수는 진정한 구조적 상태 의존성을 포착하는가, 아니면 단순히 지속적인 미관찰 이질성을 흡수하는 것에 불과한가? 이는 이후 혼합 로짓과 위계적 베이즈 연구가 직접 해결하고자 했던 식별 상의 혼란 변수이다.

3주차 — IIA, 중첩 로짓, GEV 모형

주제. 단순 로짓의 아킬레스건인 무관한 대안의 독립성(IIA)과, 닫힌 형태를 유지하면서 이를 완화하기 위해 구축된 일반화 극치(GEV) 모형군.

세부 주제. 레드 버스/블루 버스 문제; 비례적 대체(proportional substitution)와 그 비현실성; 상관된 대안들의 중첩(nesting); GEV 클래스와 포괄 가치(inclusive-value) 구조; 교차 탄력성 패턴.

방법론. 중첩 로짓 추정; 포괄 가치 및 비유사성 모수(dissimilarity parameter); IIA 검정; GEV 생성 함수.

핵심 문헌.

  • McFadden (1980), “Econometric Models for Probabilistic Choice Among Products,” The Journal of Business. doi:10.1086/296093 — GEV 프레임워크와 차별화된 제품 간의 대체 패턴 모델링을 개발한 구조적 수요 추정의 직계 기원. [F]
  • Guadagni & Little (1983), “A Logit Model of Brand Choice Calibrated on Scanner Data,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.2.3.203 — 밀접한 대체 브랜드들로 인해 IIA의 제약적 대체 패턴이 가장 뚜렷하게 위배되는 표준적 환경으로 재검토. [F]

토론 주제. 중첩 로짓은 사전에 지정된 트리 내에서 IIA를 수정하지만, 그 트리는 누가 선택하며 분석가가 부과한 중첩 구조는 가정을 검정하기보다 단순히 가정을 이전하는 것에 불과하지 않은가?

4주차 — 확률계수와 혼합 로짓

주제. 혼합(확률계수) 로짓: 선호 모수가 혼합 분포에 따라 개인 간에 변하도록 허용함으로써 IIA를 완전히 해소하고 모든 확률효용모형을 근사할 수 있도록 함.

세부 주제. 선호에 대한 혼합 분포; 상관된 확률계수; 유연한 대체 패턴; 반복 선택을 포함하는 패널 혼합 로짓.

방법론. 시뮬레이션 최대우도법(SML) 및 최대 시뮬레이션 우도법(MSL); Halton 추출; McFadden–Train 근사 정리.

핵심 문헌.

  • McFadden & Train (2000), “Mixed MNL Models for Discrete Response,” Journal of Applied Econometrics. doi:10.1002/1099-1255(200009/10)15:5<447::aid-jae570>3.0.co;2-1 — 혼합 로짓이 임의의 RUM 선택 확률을 임의의 정확도로 근사할 수 있음을 증명하여 전체 접근법의 이론적 정당성을 부여. [F]
  • Revelt & Train (1998), “Mixed Logit with Repeated Choices: Households’ Choices of Appliance Efficiency Level,” The Review of Economics and Statistics. doi:10.1162/003465398557735 — 가구 내 상관관계를 고려한 패널 데이터 혼합 로짓 추정의 표준 템플릿. [F]
  • Train (2009), Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press — 시뮬레이션 기반 추정을 위한 표준 대학원 교재; 단일 DOI 없이 도서로 인용. [F]

토론 주제. 혼합 분포 설정의 자유로움은 장점인가 덫인가? 잘못 지정된 모수적 혼합 법칙(예: 양의 가격 민감도를 함의하는 정규 가격 계수)은 복원하고자 하는 이질성 자체를 왜곡하지 않는가?

5주차 — 이질성과 위계적 베이즈

주제. 위계적 사전분포(hierarchical prior)를 통해 소비자 전반의 정보를 풀링(pooling)하여 개인 수준 선호 모수를 추정: 혼합 로짓의 베이지안 대응물이며 마케팅 이질성 전통의 핵심 도구.

세부 주제. 변량효과/위계적 사전분포; 모집단 평균으로의 수축(shrinkage); 타겟팅을 위한 개인 수준 사후분포; 구매 이력의 가치.

방법론. 위계적 베이즈; 깁스 샘플링(Gibbs sampling) 및 데이터 증강(data augmentation); 다변량 정규 이질성 분포; 개인별 추정치로서의 사후 평균.

핵심 문헌.

  • Allenby & Rossi (1998), “Marketing Models of Consumer Heterogeneity,” Journal of Econometrics. doi:10.1016/S0304-4076(98)00055-4 — 이질성을 단순한 골칫거리가 아닌 핵심 관심 대상으로 다루고 이를 복원하기 위한 위계적 베이즈 체계를 제시한 선언문적 논문. [F]
  • Rossi, McCulloch & Allenby (1996), “The Value of Purchase History Data in Target Marketing,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.15.4.321 — 개인 수준 사후분포가 타겟팅을 어떻게 정교화하는지 보여주며 이질성 추정의 상업적 가치를 입증. [F]

토론 주제. 개인 수준 사후분포는 실제 이질성을 복원하는가, 아니면 개인당 희소한 데이터 위에 모수적 사전분포를 단순히 투영하는 것에 불과한가? 사전분포가 결과를 지배하지 않으려면 얼마나 많은 구매 이력이 필요한가?

6주차 — 컨조인트 분석과 선호 측정

주제. 시장 데이터 대신 설계된 선택 실험으로부터 선호를 도출: 현시 선호(revealed-preference) 수요 추정을 보완하는 진술 선호(stated-preference) 측정법.

세부 주제. 전체 프로파일(full-profile) 대 선택 기반 컨조인트(CBC); 실험 설계 및 속성 균형; 부분가치(part-worth) 효용; 컨조인트에서 선택 시뮬레이터 및 지불의사액(WTP)으로의 연결.

방법론. 설계된 요인/부분요인 실험; (위계적 베이즈) 로짓으로 추정되는 선택 기반 컨조인트; 신뢰도 및 외적 타당도.

핵심 문헌.

  • Green & Srinivasan (1978), “Conjoint Analysis in Consumer Research: Issues and Outlook,” Journal of Consumer Research. doi:10.1086/208721 — 컨조인트를 마케팅의 대표적 선호 측정 방법론으로 확립한 기념비적 개괄 논문. [F]
  • Green & Srinivasan (1990), “Conjoint Analysis in Marketing: New Developments with Implications for Research and Practice,” Journal of Marketing. doi:10.1177/002224299005400402 — RUM과 호환되는 선택 기반 설계로 컨조인트를 재정립한 10년 주기 후속 연구. [F]

토론 주제. 가상 선택에서 도출된 진술 선호는 시장 선택에서 도출된 현시 선호와 동일한 모수를 복원하는가? 가상 편향(hypothetical bias)으로 인해 컨조인트 기반 지불의사액이 신뢰할 수 없는 수요 입력값이 되는 시점은 언제인가?

7주차 — 집계 수요와 BLP 모형

주제. 개인 선택에서 집계 수요로의 결정적 전환: 개인 데이터가 부재하고 가격이 내생적인 상황에서 시장 수준 점유율로부터 구조적 수요 모수를 복원.

세부 주제. 관찰되지 않는 제품 품질 항; 시장점유율 역변환; 시장 수준에서의 확률계수; 가격에 대한 도구변수 설정.

방법론. Berry 역변환(점유율에서 평균 효용으로); BLP 축약사상(contraction mapping); 수요측 도구변수를 활용한 일반화적률법(GMM).

핵심 문헌.

  • Berry (1994), “Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation,” The RAND Journal of Economics. doi:10.2307/2555829 — 집계 수요 문제를 평균 효용 공간에서의 선형 도구변수 문제로 전환하는 점유율 역변환 개념을 도입. [F]
  • Berry, Levinsohn & Pakes (1995), “Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium,” Econometrica. doi:10.2307/2171802 — 공급측 균형을 결합한 완전한 확률계수 집계 수요 모형을 제시; 당대 가장 영향력 있는 수요 연구. [F]

토론 주제. BLP 도구변수(경쟁사 제품 특성, 비용 변동 요인)는 제품 특성이 관찰되지 않는 품질 \(\xi\)에 대해 외생적이라는 가정에 의존한다. 기업이 \(\xi\)를 알고 제품을 설계할 때 이 가정은 과연 타당한가? 추정량으로서의 BLP 수요 모형에서는 이 추정량과 제외 제약(exclusion restriction)을 상세히 다룬다.

8주차 — BLP의 실무 적용

주제. 확률계수 집계 수요를 실제로 추정하는 기법: 신뢰할 수 있는 BLP 추정치와 불안정한 추정치를 가르는 수치해석, 도구변수, 식별 상의 선택들.

세부 주제. 도구변수의 선택과 약한 도구변수(weak instruments) 문제; 내부 축약 루프와 외부 GMM 루프; 수치적 함정과 수렴성; 수요로부터 복원되는 시장 지배력 및 마크업.

방법론. 중첩 고정점(nested fixed-point) GMM; 최적 도구변수; 공급측 가격 책정 적률 조건; 시리얼 산업에의 응용.

핵심 문헌.

  • Nevo (2000), “A Practitioner’s Guide to Estimation of Random-Coefficients Logit Models of Demand,” Journal of Economics & Management Strategy. doi:10.1162/105864000567954 — 한 세대의 연구자들이 BLP를 실제로 추정할 수 있도록 안내한 교육적 지침서. [F]
  • Nevo (2001), “Measuring Market Power in the Ready-to-Eat Cereal Industry,” Econometrica. doi:10.1111/1468-0262.00194 — 추정된 수요로부터 마크업과 시장 지배력을 복원한 표준적 BLP 응용 연구. [R]

토론 주제. BLP 추정치 중 얼마만큼이 도구변수에 의해 식별되고 얼마만큼이 모수적 함수 형태 및 분포 가정에 의해 식별되는가? 실무 지침서는 수치해석적 취약성을 과소평가하고 있는 것은 아닌가?

9주차 — 동적 수요: 비축과 내구재

주제. 정적 벤치마크의 완화: 소비자가 미래지향적(forward-looking)일 때 오늘의 수요는 예상되는 미래 가격에 의존하므로, 가격 인하는 구매 수준뿐만 아니라 구매 시점을 이동시킨다.

세부 주제. 저장 가능한 재화의 재고 및 비축; 가격 하락 상황에서 내구재의 미래지향적 채택; 기간 간 대체(intertemporal substitution)와 진정한 수요 확장의 구별; 동적 이산 선택 해결 방법.

방법론. 수요 모형 내 동적 프로그래밍/벨만 가치 함수; 기대 형성의 추정; 조건부 선택 확률(CCP) 및 중첩 고정점 추정량.

핵심 문헌.

  • Erdem & Keane (1996), “Decision-Making Under Uncertainty: Capturing Dynamic Brand Choice Processes in Turbulent Consumer Goods Markets,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.15.1.1 — 브랜드 선택에 미래지향적 학습과 불확실성을 도입하여 마케팅의 동적 구조 모형 전통을 확립. [F]
  • Hendel & Nevo (2006), “Measuring the Implications of Sales and Consumer Inventory Behavior,” Econometrica. doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00721.x — 비축 행태를 무시할 경우 정적 수요 탄력성과 장기적 정책 결론이 편향됨을 입증. [F]
  • Gowrisankaran & Rysman (2012), “Dynamics of Consumer Demand for New Durable Goods,” Journal of Political Economy. doi:10.1086/669540 — 가격 하락과 품질 향상이 수반되는 내구재에 대한 다루기 쉬운 동적 BLP 모형을 제시. [R]

토론 주제. 동적 수요 모형은 연구자가 관찰할 수 없는 소비자 기대를 필요로 한다. 합리적 기대 가정이 유효한 기여를 하는가, 아니면 도출하고자 하는 결론을 사전에 주입하는 것에 불과한가?

10주차 — 탐색과 고려군

주제. 완전정보 가정의 완화: 소비자는 전체 구색을 평가하지 않고 비용이 드는 탐색을 통해 고려군(consideration set)을 형성하므로, 관찰된 선택은 내생적이고 잠재적인 부분집합에서의 선택이다.

세부 주제. 고려군 형성; 순차적 탐색 대 동시적 탐색; 인지도 변화 요인으로서의 광고; 선택 및 탐색 데이터로부터 탐색 비용의 식별.

방법론. 구조적 탐색 모형; 고려 후 선택 2단계 모형; 선택 패턴 및 (가용한 경우) 탐색 데이터로부터 고려군 식별.

핵심 문헌.

  • Roberts & Lattin (1991), “Development and Testing of a Model of Consideration Set Composition,” Journal of Marketing Research. doi:10.2307/3172783 — 고려군 형성과 이것이 선택에 미치는 영향을 마케팅 분야에서 조기에 정식화. [F]
  • Mehta, Rajiv & Srinivasan (2003), “Price Uncertainty and Consumer Search: A Structural Model of Consideration Set Formation,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.22.1.58.12849 — 가격에 대한 비용 수반 탐색을 구조적 선택 모형 내에 통합. [R]
  • Honka, Hortaçsu & Vitorino (2017), “Advertising, Consumer Awareness, and Choice: Evidence from the U.S. Banking Industry,” The RAND Journal of Economics. doi:10.1111/1756-2171.12188 — 인지도, 고려, 선택 단계를 분리하여 식별하고 광고가 인지도 단계에 미치는 영향을 규명. [R]

토론 주제. 고려군은 잠재적이다. 탐색 데이터 없이 연구자가 “고려되지 않음”과 “고려되었으나 기각됨”을 구별할 수 있는가, 아니면 식별이 전적으로 함수 형태에 의존하는가?

11주차 — 선택 모형에서의 내생성

주제. 세미나의 핵심 식별 문제: 가격(및 기타 마케팅 믹스 변수)이 관찰되지 않는 수요 변동 요인과 상관관계를 가져 모든 반사실적 분석이 의존하는 가격 계수를 편향시킴.

세부 주제. 비집계 수준에서의 가격 내생성; 통제 함수 대 도구변수; 외부 도구변수 없는 코퓰러 기반 교정; 관찰되지 않는 제품 특성.

방법론. 통제 함수(2단계 잔차 포함법) 추정; 가우시안 코퓰러 방법; 도구변수 구축 및 타당성 검정.

핵심 문헌.

  • Villas-Boas & Winer (1999), “Endogeneity in Brand Choice Models,” Management Science. doi:10.1287/mnsc.45.10.1324 — 스캐너 데이터에서 가격 내생성을 무시할 경우 브랜드 선택 탄력성이 왜곡됨을 실증. [F]
  • Petrin & Train (2010), “A Control Function Approach to Endogeneity in Consumer Choice Models,” Journal of Marketing Research. doi:10.1509/jmkr.47.1.3 — 개인 수준에서 BLP 스타일 도구변수를 대체하는 통제 함수 접근법을 제시. [R]
  • Park & Gupta (2012), “Handling Endogenous Regressors by Joint Estimation Using Copulas,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.1120.0718 — 내생적 회귀변수의 비정규성을 활용하여 외부 도구변수 없이 내생성을 교정. [R]

토론 주제. 코퓰러 방법은 도구변수 대신 분포 가정(비정규 회귀변수, 정규 오차)으로부터 식별을 도출한다. 제외 제약을 분포 제약으로 맞바꾸는 것은 진정한 발전인가, 아니면 가정을 재명명한 것에 불과한가?

12주차 — 베이지안 추정과 MCMC

주제. 풍부하고 이질적인 선택 모형을 추정 가능하게 만드는 베이지안 계산 도구: 이산 선택 우도 함수에 적용되는 데이터 증강, 깁스 샘플링, 메트로폴리스-헤이스팅스(Metropolis–Hastings) 알고리즘.

세부 주제. 프로빗/로짓에 대한 데이터 증강; 켤레 위계적 사전분포(conjugate hierarchical priors); 믹싱(mixing) 및 수렴 진단; 다양성 추구 수요 및 코너 솔루션(corner solutions).

방법론. 잠재 효용 증강을 결합한 깁스 샘플링; 비켤레 블록에 대한 랜덤 워크 메트로폴리스-헤이스팅스; 이질적 모수에 대한 위계적 사전분포.

핵심 문헌.

  • Rossi, Allenby & McCulloch (2005), Bayesian Statistics and Marketing, Wiley — 베이지안 계산과 마케팅 선택 모형을 결합한 표준 지침서; 단일 DOI 없이 도서로 인용. [F]
  • Allenby, Arora & Ginter (1998), “On the Heterogeneity of Demand,” Journal of Marketing Research. doi:10.2307/3152035 — 위계적 베이즈 이질성 복원과 그 경영학적 함의를 실제로 구현하여 제시. [F]
  • Kim, Allenby & Rossi (2002), “Modeling Consumer Demand for Variety,” Marketing Science. doi:10.1287/mksc.21.3.229.143 — 단일 단위 선택을 넘어 다중 이산성(multiple-discreteness) 및 코너 솔루션으로 베이지안 선택 모형을 확장. [R]

토론 주제. 동일한 혼합 로짓에 대한 베이지안 추정량과 고전적(시뮬레이션 우도) 추정량은 점근적으로 동등하다. 그렇다면 둘 사이의 선택은 실질적인 것인가 단순한 계산상의 문제인가? 사전분포가 결론을 실질적으로 바꾸는 경우는 언제인가?

13주차 — 머신러닝과 수요 모형

주제. 머신러닝의 프론티어: 유연한 수요 예측 및 데이터 기반의 이질적 반응 복원이 구조적 수요 추정과 갖는 긴장 및 상호작용.

세부 주제. 유연한/비모수적 수요 예측 및 모형 결합; 재귀적 분할(recursive partitioning)을 통한 이질적 처치 효과 추정; 대규모 구색에 대한 제품 선택 딥러닝 모형; 예측 대 구조적 식별.

방법론. 정규화 및 앙상블 예측; 처치 효과 이질성을 위한 인과/정직 나무(causal/honest trees) 및 포레스트; 신경망 선택 모형.

핵심 문헌.

  • Bajari, Nekipelov, Ryan & Yang (2015), “Machine Learning Methods for Demand Estimation,” American Economic Review (Papers & Proceedings). doi:10.1257/aer.p20151021 — 표본 외 적합도 측면에서 머신러닝 예측기와 구조적 수요 모형을 벤치마킹. [R]
  • Athey & Imbens (2016), “Recursive Partitioning for Heterogeneous Causal Effects,” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. doi:10.1073/pnas.1510489113 — 타당한 통계적 추론을 유지하며 이질적 마케팅 반응을 복원하는 인과 나무 방법론을 제시. [R]
  • Gabel & Timoshenko (2022), “Product Choice with Large Assortments: A Scalable Deep-Learning Model,” Management Science. doi:10.1287/mnsc.2021.3969 — 고전적 로짓이 다룰 수 있는 범위를 넘어서는 대규모 구색으로 확장 가능한 신경망 선택 모형을 제안. [R]

토론 주제. 머신러닝은 예측에는 탁월하지만 반사실적 분석에는 침묵한다. 유연한 예측기가 구조적 수요 모형의 본래 목적인 가격 탄력성과 후생 적분값을 도출할 수 있는가, 아니면 서로 다른 질문에 답하고 있는가?

14주차 — 후생 분석, 반사실적 평가 및 종합

주제. 세미나 여정의 종착점: 수요 체계는 후생 및 반사실적 분석을 계산하기 위해 존재하므로, 신제품의 효익, 기업 결합 효과, 그리고 추정된 수요가 측정 가능하게 해주는 소비자 잉여를 종합 평가한다.

세부 주제. 로짓 포괄 가치로부터의 보상 변위(compensating variation); 신제품 및 다양성의 후생 가치; 기업 결합 시뮬레이션; 후생 분석에서 선호 이질성을 무시할 때 발생하는 편향.

방법론. 추정된 수요로부터의 소비자 잉여 계산; 반사실적 균형 시뮬레이션; 로그합(log-sum) 후생 공식.

핵심 문헌.

  • Petrin (2002), “Quantifying the Benefits of New Products: The Case of the Minivan,” Journal of Political Economy. doi:10.1086/340779 — 추정된 BLP 수요를 활용하여 제품 혁신에 따른 소비자 후생 증가를 계산함으로써 전체 연구 프로그램의 전형적 결실을 입증. [F]
  • Trajtenberg (1989), “The Welfare Analysis of Product 혁신s, with an Application to Computed Tomography Scanners,” Journal of Political Economy. doi:10.1086/261611 — 신제품 문헌의 효시가 된 혁신에 대한 초기 이산 선택 후생 분석. [F]
  • Nevo (2001), “Measuring Market Power in the Ready-to-Eat Cereal Industry,” Econometrica. doi:10.1111/1468-0262.00194 — 추정된 수요로부터 마크업을 복원하고 합병 효과를 시뮬레이션한 대표적 반사실적 분석 사례로 재검토. [R]

토론 주제. 반사실적 후생 수치는 수요 모형의 모든 전제 가정을 그대로 상속받는다. 그 크기가 선호 분포의 식별되지 않은 꼬리 부분에 의존하는 잉여 추정치를 규제 당국이나 경영진이 얼마나 신뢰해야 하는가?

기초 고전 대 최신 프론티어 한눈에 보기

선택 및 수요 연구자가 철저히 숙지해야 할 기초 고전(foundational core)은 확률효용 미시적 기초에서부터 집계 수요 혁명에 이르기까지 이어진다. RUM 및 GEV 확장을 다룬 Thurstone (1927), Luce (1959), McFadden (1974, 1980); 스캐너 선택 응용을 다룬 Guadagni & Little (1983)과 Gupta (1988); 혼합 로짓을 다룬 McFadden & Train (2000)과 Revelt & Train (1998); 위계적 베이즈 이질성을 다룬 Allenby & Rossi (1998)와 Rossi, McCulloch & Allenby (1996); 선호 측정을 다룬 Green & Srinivasan (1978, 1990); 집계 수요를 다룬 Berry (1994)와 Berry, Levinsohn & Pakes (1995); 동적 모형을 다룬 Erdem & Keane (1996)과 Hendel & Nevo (2006); 내생성을 다룬 Villas-Boas & Winer (1999); 그리고 후생 분석을 다룬 Petrin (2002)과 Trajtenberg (1989)가 이에 해당한다. 이들은 해당 분야의 박사학위 논문이라면 별도의 설명 없이도 인용해야 하는 핵심 저작들이다.

매 개정판마다 갱신되는 최신 프론티어(frontier)는 학계의 활발한 최신 동향을 추적한다. 응용 및 동적 BLP를 다룬 Nevo (2001)와 Gowrisankaran & Rysman (2012); 구조적 탐색과 고려군을 다룬 Mehta, Rajiv & Srinivasan (2003)과 Honka, Hortaçsu & Vitorino (2017); 내생성 교정을 다룬 Petrin & Train (2010)과 Park & Gupta (2012); 다중 이산성을 다룬 Kim, Allenby & Rossi (2002); 그리고 머신러닝과의 접점을 다룬 Bajari et al. (2015), Athey & Imbens (2016), Gabel & Timoshenko (2022) 등이 포함된다. 이러한 구분은 연대기적인 것이 아니라 교육적인 것이다. 1995년 논문은 그 역변환과 GMM에 학계가 여전히 기반을 두고 있기에 기초 고전인 반면, 2016년 방법론은 구조적 수요와의 결합이 여전히 활발히 진행 중이므로 프론티어로 분류된다.

본 장의 확장 방향

주차별 리딩 맵은 향후 다음과 같은 여러 축을 따라 확장될 수 있도록 설계되었다.

  1. 프론티어 모듈의 2~3년 주기 갱신. 머신러닝, 동적 수요, 탐색 모듈은 변화가 가장 빠르므로, 기초 닻(RUM, Berry 역변환, 혼합 로짓)은 유지하되 새로운 방법론과 응용이 등장함에 따라 프론티어 문헌을 교체하거나 보강한다.
  2. 분야 성장에 따른 신규 모듈 추가: 대규모 머신러닝 수요 추정(정규화 및 앙상블 수요 체계, 수요 모수의 이중/비편향 추정); 제품과 소비자를 학습된 잠재 공간에 표현하여 새로운 식별 문제를 제기하는 LLM 및 임베딩 기반 선호 모형; 프라이버시 제약 및 차분 프라이버시(differentially private) 데이터 하에서의 수요 추정. 각 모듈은 기초 닻, 프론티어 논문, 식별 상의 토론이라는 기존 템플릿을 따른다.
  3. 병렬 방법론 축의 보강. 각 모듈은 이미 식별 가정(극치 오차, 중첩 트리, 혼합 분포, BLP 제외 제약, 합리적 기대, 코퓰러의 분포 가정)을 명시하고 있다. 향후 개정판에서는 매주 추정량, 적률 조건 또는 우도 함수, 식별을 저해하는 요인을 명시하는 요약본을 추가하여, 아래의 BLP 실습 섹션처럼 리딩 맵을 완전한 방법론 코스로 발전시킬 수 있다.
  4. 응용 트랙의 구축. 각 추정량을 표준 산업 사례(자동차, 시리얼, 내구재, 은행업, 소매 구색)와 연결하여, 학생들이 서로 다른 외생적 변량 원천을 갖는 다양한 환경에서 동일한 방법론이 어떻게 식별되는지 확인할 수 있도록 한다.

다음 절에서는 본 리딩 맵이 지향하는 실질적인 추정 예제를 제공한다.

추정량으로서의 BLP 수요 모형

Berry (1994) 및 Berry–Levinsohn–Pakes (1995) 모형은 본 세미나 전체의 핵심 축이다. 이 모형은 확률효용 논리를 개인 선택에서 집계 수요로 확장하며 가격 내생성 문제를 정면으로 다룬다. 여기서는 추정량, 그 역변환, 그리고 식별의 기반이 되는 핵심 가정을 수식으로 정리한다.

시장 \(t\)에서 소비자 \(i\)가 제품 \(j\)로부터 얻는 효용은 다음과 같다. \[ u_{ijt} = \mathbf{x}_{jt}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\beta}_i - \alpha_i\, p_{jt} + \xi_{jt} + \varepsilon_{ijt}, \tag{199.1}\] 여기서 \(\mathbf{x}_{jt}\)는 관찰된 특성 벡터, \(p_{jt}\)는 가격, \(\xi_{jt}\)는 시장 \(t\)에서 (연구자에게) 관찰되지 않는 제품 품질이며, \(\varepsilon_{ijt}\)는 i.i.d. 극치 선호 충격이다. 확률계수 \((\boldsymbol{\beta}_i, \alpha_i)\)는 모수적 분포에 따라 소비자 간에 변동하며, 예컨대 \((\boldsymbol{\beta}_i,\alpha_i) = (\bar{\boldsymbol{\beta}},\bar\alpha) + \boldsymbol{\Sigma}\,\boldsymbol{\nu}_i\)이고 \(\boldsymbol{\nu}_i \sim \Phi\)이다. 외부 재화(outside good) \(j=0\)의 효용은 \(u_{i0t}=\varepsilon_{i0t}\)로 정규화된다.

선호 분포에 대해 로짓 선택 확률을 적분하면 모형이 예측하는 제품 \(j\)의 시장점유율을 얻는다. \[ s_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\delta}_t,\boldsymbol{\theta}_2) = \int \frac{\exp\!\big(\delta_{jt} + \mu_{ijt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2)\big)} {1 + \sum_{k} \exp\!\big(\delta_{kt} + \mu_{ikt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2)\big)} \, d\Phi(\boldsymbol{\nu}), \tag{199.2}\] 여기서 \(\delta_{jt} = \mathbf{x}_{jt}^{\top}\bar{\boldsymbol{\beta}} - \bar\alpha\,p_{jt} + \xi_{jt}\)는 제품 \(j\)의 평균 효용(mean utility)이며, \(\mu_{ijt}\)는 이질성 모수 \(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2=\mathrm{vec}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma})\)에 의해 제어되는 개인별 편차를 모은 것이다. 이 적분은 닫힌 형태가 없으므로 \(\boldsymbol{\nu}_i\)의 시뮬레이션 추출을 통해 근사된다.

Berry (1994)의 핵심 결과는 \(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2\)를 고정했을 때 평균 효용에서 점유율로의 매핑이 역변환 가능(invertible)하다는 점이다. 즉, 예측 점유율을 관찰된 점유율 \(\mathbf{S}_t\)와 일치시키는 유일한 벡터 \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_t\)가 존재한다. BLP는 이를 다음과 같은 축약사상(contraction mapping)의 고정점으로 계산한다. \[ \delta_{jt}^{(r+1)} = \delta_{jt}^{(r)} + \ln S_{jt} - \ln s_{jt}\!\big(\boldsymbol{\delta}_t^{(r)},\boldsymbol{\theta}_2\big), \tag{199.3}\] 이를 수렴할 때까지 반복한다. 이 역변환은 집계 수요 문제를 \(\xi\)에 대해 선형인 모형으로 전환시킨다. 일단 \(\boldsymbol{\delta}_t(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2)\)가 복원되면 구조적 오차는 다음과 같이 정의된다. \[ \xi_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \delta_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_2) - \mathbf{x}_{jt}^{\top}\bar{\boldsymbol{\beta}} + \bar\alpha\, p_{jt}. \tag{199.4}\]

추정은 GMM을 통해 진행된다. 가격 \(p_{jt}\)는 관찰되지 않는 품질 \(\xi_{jt}\)와 상관되어 있으므로(기업은 \(\xi\)가 높은 제품에 더 높은 가격을 책정함), \(\delta\)를 가격에 대해 단순 회귀분석하면 편향이 발생한다. 따라서 식별을 위해서는 다음의 모집단 적률 조건을 만족하는 도구변수 벡터 \(\mathbf{z}_{jt}\)가 필요하다. \[ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\, \xi_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_0)\,\big|\, \mathbf{z}_{jt} \right] = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb{E}\!\left[\, \mathbf{z}_{jt}\, \xi_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_0)\,\right]=0, \tag{199.5}\] 추정량은 가중 행렬 \(\mathbf{W}\)를 사용하여 이에 대응하는 표본 적률을 최소화한다. \[ \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\; \Big(\tfrac{1}{N}\textstyle\sum_{jt}\mathbf{z}_{jt}\,\xi_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\Big)^{\!\top} \mathbf{W} \Big(\tfrac{1}{N}\textstyle\sum_{jt}\mathbf{z}_{jt}\,\xi_{jt}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\Big). \tag{199.6}\] 표준적인 도구변수로는 비용 변동 요인(cost shifters)과 경쟁 제품 특성의 함수(BLP 도구변수)가 사용되며, 이들은 해당 제품의 자체 수요에는 직접 들어가지 않으면서 경쟁 구도를 통해 가격과 마크업을 변화시킨다. Figure 199.3는 내부 축약 루프와 외부 GMM 탐색으로 이루어진 이 추정량의 중첩 구조를 종합한 것이다.
